subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THE DEFECT, reported by the GW lane and fixed here. webfrank's window relocation hash packed the raw ELF r_info, which embeds the SYMBOL TABLE INDEX — a TU-GLOBAL quantity. So adding or dropping any symbol ANYWHERE in a translation unit renumbered it and hard-aborted that whole TU's build against every instruction_permutation pin, with an error ('relocation input hash changed') that reads like the unrelated edit's fault. GW measured it on gauntworld::fn_8005FB48: a _savefpr change moved indices 339->341 and 337->339 while both text hashes were unchanged and every relocation kept its offset, type, addend and symbol NAME.

THE FIX. Hash the relocation TYPE (the low byte of r_info) plus the SYMBOL NAME, plus offset and addend — the quantities the rules' own prose already reasons about. Names are MANDATORY whenever a relocation is present: dropping the index without substituting the name would leave the hash blind to a re-symboling, which is a weaker guard, not a friendlier one.

WHY THE MIGRATION WAS CHEAP, and how it was audited. The empty-list hash is unchanged, so only windows that actually carry a relocation needed re-stamping: 22 of 46 windows across 39 permutation rules, 42 hash values. The audit that made it safe was NOT the rewrite but the pre-check — for every one of the 46 windows the STORED hash was first confirmed to equal what the LEGACY index-based scheme computes from today's objects (46 checked, 0 misaligned), which proves the file-order traversal is aligned and that nothing else had drifted; the rewrite then touched only the two hash string values per window, leaving text hashes untouched, and the full ninja replayed all 39 permutation rules to 'build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK' with the exact count unchanged. A hash-value-keyed rewrite must also refuse when one old value maps to two different new values; that check found no collisions here but is the thing that would silently corrupt a rule.

SIDE FINDING, worth knowing before authoring one. A post_recolor_permutation window's stored before/after relocation hashes are DEAD DATA: that stage passes [] and computes the empty hash itself, ignoring whatever the rule stores. One shipped window (game/world/camera::camera_mode_level [0x8c0,0x8c8)) carries non-empty values there that nothing reads.
